extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, marketers, communications managers, and small-business owners who write and distribute press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, data-driven guidance for increasing the likelihood a press release will be picked up by media: covers timing, targeting, multimedia, outreach windows, and elements of newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline pickup rate (expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only 2-3% of press releases result in media pickup across all industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a realistic baseline expectation when planning campaigns and KPIs; most releases will not become news stories, so measure success against low industry norms and focus on tactics to improve above this baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted distribution to specific industry sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: 67% higher pickup rates for releases focused on specific industry sectors vs. broad distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer narrow, sector-specific mailing lists and distribution channels rather than blanket broad lists. Tailor messaging to the recipients' beat/industry to increase relevance and pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include at least one executive quote
rubrics_metrics.description: 40% higher pickup rates for releases with at least one executive quote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a concise, attributable executive quote that provides perspective or a human angle. Avoid boilerplate or generic quotes; make them newsworthy and directly related to the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimal general distribution timing (day and hour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuesday and Wednesday mornings (8:00-9:00 AM local time): 30% more media attention. Avoid Mondays, Fridays, and weekends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule general press-distribution sends for Tuesday/Wednesday 8–9 AM local time to align with journalists' news cycles. Avoid Monday (catch-up) and Friday/weekends (winding down) for broad distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email outreach engagement window (direct journalist contact)
rubrics_metrics.description: 10:00 AM - 2:00 PM = ~45% click-through rate; best window for direct journalist outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When emailing individual journalists, target the 10 AM–2 PM local window to maximize open/click probability. This window is especially important for personalized pitches rather than mass distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct, personalized journalist outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct journalist outreach via email increases pickup likelihood; contacts should be personalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on mass distribution. Personalize pitches to a journalist's beat and include relevant hooks; use the email engagement window above. Avoid generic, untargeted copy that reads like a mass blast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include high-quality multimedia (images, video, immersive assets)
rubrics_metrics.description: 94% increase in views with multimedia; 650% increase in engagement with visuals; 3x more interaction for releases with video; immersive multimedia yields a 48% increase in social sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed or attach high-resolution images and, where relevant, video or immersive assets. Ensure visuals are professional, captioned, and relevant. Leverage multiple asset types to cater to different outlet formats (web, social, broadcast).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide multiple multimedia assets (≥3 recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: 6x higher engagement with multiple visual assets vs text-only; the implicit rubric recommends having ≥3 multimedia assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply a package of at least three varied assets (e.g., hero image, additional photos, short video, infographic) so editors and social teams can choose the best format. Multiple assets increase usage flexibility and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design shareable visual elements and social-ready content
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual content drives social amplification: 94% higher social engagement for visuals; Facebook images get more likes/comments, tweets with images get nearly 2x retweets; visual content can be 40x more likely to be shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include social-sized images, short video clips, and ready-to-share graphics. Add captions, suggested social copy, and 'tweetable' lines to make it easy for outlets and audiences to share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include clear 'tweetable' facts or soundbites
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should have clear 'tweetable' facts to increase shareability and quick uptake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide one-line, pithy facts or statistics formatted for social sharing (short, specific, and quotable). These should be accurate and linked to source data where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the headline tell a story
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic question: Does the headline tell a story?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a headline that conveys the news Hook and key takeaway in one sentence. Avoid vague or overly promotional headlines; prioritize specificity and news value to entice editors and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a strong news hook / ensure genuine newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic questions: Is the news genuinely newsworthy? Is there a strong news hook?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the announcement has timeliness, relevance, human interest, novelty, or impact. Explicitly state the hook early in the release (lead paragraph) to communicate why journalists should cover it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use compelling facts and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Diagnostic question: Are facts and statistics compelling?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims with specific, verifiable numbers and context. Use third-party data or clear internal metrics to add credibility. Avoid vague assertions without supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing/alignment between distribution and outreach channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Different timing recommendations apply to mass distribution (Tue/Wed 8–9 AM) vs. direct email outreach (10 AM–2 PM); alignment matters for pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate your mass distribution schedule with personalized outreach so journalists receive the most relevant material at the optimal time for their workflow. Plan follow-ups within the same day-window where appropriate.
